children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose more than 4% on Monday to notch their highest close since late July, as chipmakers rallied on optimism around strong demand for AI investments.
** The won hit its highest level in nearly two years, while the benchmark bond yield rose.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed up 308.18 points, or 4.61%, at 6,995.39, its highest closing level since July 23 and the biggest daily percentage rise since August 20.
** Wall Street weakened on Friday, but the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
was a clear outperformer, gaining 3.4%.
** South Korea's exports so far this year have already surpassed last year's annual record, as the economy rides high on booming global demand for AI chips.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 5.68% and peer SK Hynix
gained 8.26%, leading the benchmark index higher.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 1.12%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were up 2.48% and up 1.50%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 0.45%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
rose 1.31%.
** Of the total 911 traded issues, 478 shares advanced, while 381 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 2.6 trillion won ($1.94 billion).
** The won was quoted at 1,340.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.72% higher than its previous close at 1,350.1. Earlier in the session, it rose as much as 1.15% to 1,334.7, its strongest level since early October 2024.
** South Korea's National Pension Service (NPS) has suspended foreign exchange hedging operations, as the won strengthened to a near two-year high.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on 3-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.04 of a point to 103.13.
** The most liquid 3-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 2.1 basis points to 3.904%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
rose by 2 basis points to 4.381%.
